articles.title: Recital del Kids&Us Manresa ante un flojo Roma Basketball (108-88)
articles.standfirst: Benite (24+5+7), Ongenda (20+7) y Oriola (19+3) y Bassas (13+5 asistencias), destacados
articles.summary: Benite (24+5+7), Ongenda (20+7) y Oriola (19+3) y Bassas (13+5 asistencias), destacados
articles.body: El Kids&Us Manresa se divirtió ante un flojo BC Roma después de derrotar con contundencia a los italianos por 108-88 en un choque dominado de principio a fin por los de Diego Ocampo. La tripleta formada por el base Hugo Benitez y los pívots Pierre Oriola y Nick Ongenda (63 puntos en total entre ellos) fue clave para que su equipo lograra una victoria plácida con un 'basket-average' que puede ser clave en futuros hipotéticos empates en la clasificación de la fase de grupos. Los primeros minutos de partido fueron los únicos donde los romanos tuvieron un acierto notable en ataque gracias a unos buenos minutos del exbaskonista Nico Mannion, que empezó bien desde la línea de tres (12-13, min. 5). Sin embargo, desde ese instante, los manresanos fueron muy superiores, especialmente en el juego interior. El primero en destacar fue Nick Ongenda, que con su habitual juego de pies, puso en problemas a la defensa de los visitantes y abrió la primera gran ventaja del encuentro (23-14, min. 7). Los locales no sólo mantuvieron la ventaja en los minutos posteriores, sino que también fueron capaces de aumentarla y finalmente acabaron con un 32-21 al final del primer cuarto. El guión no cambió en el segundo periodo, y el Kids&Us Manresa continuó con su superioridad bajo aros, pero ahora con otro protagonista, Pierre Oriola, que anotó tanto cerca de la canasta como desde el triple (41-29, min. 13). El BC Roma intentó rebajar la desventaja lo antes posible, pero cuando lo consiguió, de nuevo apareció el propio Oriola para volver al +10 y hacer daño a los italianos, que vieron como la velocidad del rival era superior a la suya (50-40, min. 18). En un cuarto con tanta anotación, los catalanes mantuvieron la ventaja y se fueron al descanso con 57 puntos anotados, frente a los 46 de los romanos, por lo que la afición manresana pudo disfrutar más que en los partidos anteriores. En la reanudación, el Kids&Us Manresa puso la sexta marcha en el acelerador y en un abrir y cerrar de ojos logró una ventaja de 15 puntos tras otro triple, esta vez de Ferran Bassas (70-55, min. 25). Sin embargo, cuando parecía que los catalanes podían romper el partido, el BC Roma encontró el acierto desde el triple gracias a Davis Jr, e incluso lograron ponerse por debajo de los diez puntos de desventaja, situación que provocó el tiempo muerto de Ocampo (74-65, min. 28). Desde entonces, un intercambio de canastas reinó en el Nou Congost, que finalmente benefició a los locales tras los últimos fallos de los italianos, y al final el Kids&Us acabó el periodo con un 82-70 que no dejó el partido sentenciado, pero sí encarrilado. En los últimos diez minutos, los manresanos buscaron sellar el choque lo antes posible y lo consiguieron después de unos muy buenos minutos de JD Notae, que puso el 89-71 en el marcador con un BC Roma completamente hundido y sin apenas opciones de remontar. Al final, el Kids&Us Manresa, a diferencia del resto de partidos de la actual temporada, fue el equipo que se fue más allá de los 100 puntos y se llevó el triunfo por 108-88 en un duelo plácido que se traduce en la segunda victoria esta temporada en la Eurocopa. 108. BC Roma (21+25+24+18): Mannion (21), Watson (5), Strautins (10), Ayayi (12), Simonovic (4) -cinco inicial-; Davis (8), Emejuru (2), Flowers (2), Stevenson (13) y Olynyk (11). Árbitros: Uros Obrknezevic, Amit Balak y Christopher Lemaire. Sin eliminados. articles.title: LeBron James shrugs off criticism as his luxury commute becomes an NBA talking point
articles.summary: LeBron James threw down a huge dunk in his Sixers home debut and dismissed his helicopter commute as “just transportation.”
articles.body:
Few athletes live under a brighter spotlight than LeBron James. Every move he makes becomes a talking point within minutes. His new chapter in Philadelphia has already given fans plenty to talk and argue about.

One evening produced two very different conversations. One was about pure basketball joy, and the other was about logistics, money, and image. Together they show how a single big night can carry both celebration and criticism.

LeBron James took the Philadelphia floor on Friday, October 16, and performed his famous chalk toss before tipoff. A sellout crowd of 19,746 packed Xfinity Mobile Arena for the 76ers' preseason finale against Boston.

In the first quarter, Tyrese Maxey lobbed a half-court pass to James, who finished the play with a two-handed alley-oop dunk that sent the crowd into a frenzy. It offered Sixers fans an early look at the transition connection Philadelphia hopes to use this season.

James finished with 8 points, 8 rebounds and 7 assists in 25 minutes. Boston won 125-120 in overtime at Xfinity Mobile Arena, ending Philadelphia's preseason with a loss.

Tyrese Maxey started the play with a long pass in LeBron's direction. James locked eyes on the ball right away. He snared it and finished at the rim with ease for all the home fans.

Maxey is a close friend of James. LeBron has credited him with swaying the decision to sign in Philadelphia. The two now want to run the floor and score in transition as often as possible.

After the game, James said the team is still finding its rhythm. He noted they are only a couple of weeks in together. He admitted some kinks remain, but said plenty exists to build on.

On July 24, James announced that he would join Philadelphia after his agent, Rich Paul, held conversations with 27 NBA teams during the free-agency process. James agreed to a reported two-year, $8 million deal. The Sixers have not won an NBA championship since 1983.

Fanatics Fest ran from July 16-19 in New York, and James appeared at the event on July 16. Five days after the festival ended, he announced his decision to join Philadelphia. James already had a separate long-term business relationship with Fanatics through a trading-card partnership signed in 2024.

Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro proclaimed July 24 as LeBron James Day following the announcement. The designation reflected the considerable attention James' move generated across Philadelphia and Pennsylvania.

James is splitting his time between the Philadelphia area and New York City. He has used a helicopter to travel between New York and the Sixers' facilities near their Camden, New Jersey, practice site.

Front Office Sports reported that a typical one-way helicopter trip takes about 30 minutes, compared with roughly 90 minutes to 2 hours by car. Other reporting has placed the helicopter journey at approximately 30-45 minutes, depending on the trip.

The arrangement significantly reduces James' travel time between the two areas. During a demanding NBA season, avoiding lengthy road trips can free up additional time for basketball preparation, recovery, and personal commitments.

LeBron is not paying for the flights. His spokesperson told Front Office Sports that the Fanatics deal includes access to its corporate aviation. Reports say that similar trips run about $4,000 to $10,000 each way.

The arrangement also serves Fanatics. A branded helicopter carrying a global star gets attention every time it lands. Sponsors like that kind of visibility, and fans notice it quickly on social media and in headlines.

The perk also explains why the ride has become such a big topic. A famous player, a big sponsor, and a busy commute make an easy story. Fans naturally want to know exactly who pays.

Little-known fact: During a July 2026 conversation at Fanatics Fest, James explained that his growing interest in golf also connects to his broader ambitions in business and philanthropy.

After the Celtics game on Friday night, James addressed the helicopter talk for the first time. He also said he has done it before. He simply called it "Just another way of transportation. That's all."

Those were his first public comments on the rides. He is dismissing the concerns and insists it is much ado about nothing. The story had been building for over a week.

His short answer keeps the story simple. Stars often avoid long explanations when a topic feels overblown. Still, the helicopter will probably stay in the headlines every time it lifts off near Camden or Manhattan.

At 41, James is heading into a record 24th season and his first with Philadelphia. He spent the previous eight years with the Lakers. One lob and a dunk made the arena feel brand new.

Philadelphia also added Jaylen Brown by trade. He joins Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey on a roster that now threatens the reigning champion New York Knicks in the East. That depth raises expectations across Philadelphia.

One preseason game offers thin evidence. Still, James looked active as a finisher and a passer, a balance that has defined his career. It should keep Philadelphia fans very optimistic about the season ahead.

The real test begins when games count. Preseason highlights fade fast, and opponents will adjust. The Sixers must turn flashes of chemistry into steady wins across a long season of constant travel and heavy scrutiny.

The helicopter story will follow him. Each ride will invite questions about cost, safety, and focus. Winning is usually the surest way to quiet outside noise. A strong start would make the commute seem minor.

For fans, the picture is simple. A veteran legend, a speedy guard, and a hungry city make a fun mix. Whether the helicopter lands softly or loudly, the season has real buzz and big hopes.

LeBron's two-handed dunk off a Maxey pass electrified a sellout crowd of 19,746.

He calls his helicopter rides "just another way of transportation."

Fanatics covers the flights as part of his existing deal.

The Sixers now face the real test of turning chemistry into wins.

articles.title: Pistons storm back from 22-point hole to spoil Paul George’s historic Celtics debut, win NBA’s season opener
articles.summary: The NBA season tips off in Detroit as the Celtics face the Pistons.
articles.body: Paul George made history in his Boston Celtics debut. But it wasn’t enough to fend of the determined Detroit Pistons.The Pistons looked down and out at home in Tuesday’s NBA season opener as the Celtics opened a 72-50 third-quarter lead. But they stormed back to secure a stunning, 121-113 win.Sparked by Duncan Robinson and Javonte Green off the bench, the Pistons caught fire from 3 and reeled off a 23-0 fourth-quarter run to turn a 99-89 deficit into a 112-99 lead.The dizzied Celtics were out of responses. A Derrick White floater stopped the bleeding with 3:18 remaining. But the damage had been done. Detroit held on down the stretch to fire the opening salvo in what projects to be a highly competitive race in the Eastern Conference.The win spoiled a historic effort from Paul George. George led the Celtics to their 22-point lead and etched his name into Boston’s record book in the third quarter of his Celtics debut. With his 31st point in the third quarter, George set the scoring record for a player making his Celtics debut, topping Kristaps Porziņģis’ 30 points in his first game with Boston in 2023. He hit three consecutive 3-pointers in the third to extend the Boston lead. He finished with 38 points, 5 rebounds, 3 assists and 5 steals as the game’s leading scorer while shooting 12 of 21 from the field and 7 of 12 from 3. But it was Detroit’s 3-point shooting and stifling defense down the stretch that made the difference in the game.Robinson shot 5 of 9 from 3 in a 21-point effort. Green shot 5 of 8 from 3 off the bench and scored all 17 of his points in the second half after not playing in the first. A Green 3 off a Pistons defense stop capped Detroit’s 23-0 fourth-quarter run.Javonte Green misses the shot, Jayson Tatum misses the layup on the fastbreak, slow to return on defense, and Javonte hits the triple to put the Pistons up 13 pic.twitter.com/f69KksDpbd— MrBuckBuck (@MrBuckBuckNBA) October 20, 2026 In the end, the Pistons shot 17 of 42 (40.5%) from long distance after a 4-of-22 (18.2%) start to secure the comeback win.Jalen Duren tallied 22 points, 9 rebounds, 1 block and 1 steal while shooting 8 of 13 from the floor in a strong first effort since his protracted offseason contract standoff. Cade Cunningham, coming off a First-team All-NBA season, matched Duren with a team-high 22 points to go with 8 assists and 4 rebounds.While George feasted, Jayson Tatum struggled against Detroit’s stingy defense. The Celtics star finished with 13 points and 11 assists. He shot just 6 of 23 from the field and missed all seven of his 3s. He scored just two points after halftime after posting 11 in the first half.This story will be updated.

articles.title: Paul George Sets Celtics Record in Debut vs. Pistons, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Tatum, Cade
articles.summary: A historic Boston Celtics debut from Paul George wasn't enough to stop the Detroit Pistons from opening the season with a comeback victory.
articles.body:
A historic Boston Celtics debut from Paul George wasn't enough to stop the Detroit Pistons from opening the season with a comeback victory.

George set a franchise record for points in his Celtics debut before Javonte Green and the Pistons recovered from an early deficit to open the 2026-27 NBA season with a 121-113 home win.

Here's a look at some of the top performers and highlights from the first game of the 2026-27 NBA season.

George's first points as a Celtic came from behind the arc. That shot tied him for the eighth-most three pointers in NBA history, per NBA.com's Taylor Snow .

Mitchell Robinson, who had an injury scare after seemingly rolling his ankle early in the game, also recorded the first points of his Celtics career in the second quarter.

Ausar Thompson impressed on defense for the Pistons, while Cade Cunningham got off to a hot scoring start to keep the home team even with the Celtics until midway through the second quarter.

George and Tatum helped lead the Celtics on a 19-4 run in the second quarter that allowed the visitors to pull out to a 13-point lead by halftime.

He and Tatum combined for 28 points on 10-for-22 shooting through two quarters.

George passed the single-game debut points record in the third to help the Celtics stretch their lead to as many as 22 points.

The Celtics were unable to keep up that momentum after George's production slowed at the midway point of the third.

The Pistons chipped away at the deficit before going on a 23-0 run in the fourth to grab a late double-digit advantage over the visitors.

George and Derrick White took the Celtics on a seven-point run to get the visitors within four points in the final minute of regulation before the Pistons closed out the win.

The Celtics will get another chance to earn their first victory of the season as George makes his home debut against the defending champion New York Knicks. The Pistons will look to get off to a stronger start the same day at the Miami Heat.

articles.title: Mississippi Valley State basketball player released from ICE custody on bond weeks after being detained
articles.summary: Qingfang Pang, who came to the United States from China three years ago, said he was unaware he had not filed the correct paperwork to renew his visa.
articles.body:
A Mississippi Valley State basketball player who was detained by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement several weeks ago was released on bond Tuesday afternoon.

Qingfang Pang, 21, came to the United States from China three years ago and is a member of the Mississippi Valley State men's basketball team. He was arrested Sept. 29 while trying to board a flight from Jackson, Mississippi, to New York. Pang had been detained by ICE in Louisiana ever since.

Pang's attorney, Marcus Session, told ESPN on Tuesday that he was the victim of a "procedural mistake." Pang's student visa expired last month, and he was unaware that he had not filed the correct paperwork to renew it.

Then, while he was detained, Session said Peng was "coerced" into signing a voluntary departure document by ICE officials. Session said that Peng, who has a limited knowledge of the English language, didn't understand the document he was signing. It has since been rescinded, and Peng wants to remain in Mississippi.

"He legally entered the U.S. on November 17, 2023 on a temporary basis not to exceed September 5, 2024, but illegally overstayed," the U.S. Department of Homeland Security said in a statement, via ESPN . "All of his claims will be heard by an immigration judge, and he will receive due process. This administration will not ignore the rule of law."

Pang, a 6-foot-9 forward, played high school basketball in New York. He transferred into Mississippi Valley State this past offseason after getting his start at Monroe University. Mississippi Valley State officials were the ones that discovered Pang's F-1 student visa had expired, and told him he had to leave campus. Session said he was on his way to his guardian's home in New York when he was arrested at the airport.

"He's a strong kid, but even a strong kid would have his emotions and faith tested," Session said.

Peng is the second college basketball player in the United States to be detained by ICE in recent weeks. Aminata Seck, a member of the Kentucky State women's basketball team , was detained in August. Seck, who is from Senegal, was released on bond on Oct. 7.

articles.title: Jayson Tatum's Rough Stat Line in Celtics' Loss Explained by Pistons HC with 'Simple' Answer
articles.summary: Boston Celtics star Jayson Tatum had a rough open to the regular season, scoring just 13 points on 6-of-23 shooting during his team's 121-113 loss against the Detroit Pistons.
articles.body:
Boston Celtics star Jayson Tatum had a rough open to the regular season, scoring just 13 points on 6-of-23 shooting during his team's 121-113 loss against the Detroit Pistons.

Detroit head coach JB Bickerstaff offered a concise reason for Tatum's struggles.

"Ausar Thompson. That simple," he told reporters . "You get him in one-on-one situations, you're gonna be in for a long night no matter who you are."

Final Record Predictions for Every NBA Team 🔮

Tatum got off to a strong start, with 11 of his 13 points in the first half.

But the Pistons made some solid second-half adjustments while erasing a 22-point deficit in the fourth quarter.

Thompson's defense in particular continued to impress:

Thompson, 23, led the NBA in steals last season (2.0 SPG), was a first-team All-Defensive selection and finished third in the Defensive Player of the Year voting behind San Antonio's Victor Wembanyama and Oklahoma City's Chet Holmgren.

While his offensive game remains a work in progress—he finished Tuesday's opener with 11 points on 4-of-8 shooting—he made an impact on the defensive end, the boards (11 rebounds) and was a nice secondary playmaker on offense (five assists).

Tatum, meanwhile, did finish the loss with 11 assists. It's hard to imagine many games in the future where he shoots 0-for-7 from three.

And Boston will take some major positives from the game, including Paul George's monster afternoon (38 points).

Overall, a tough start for Tatum and the Celtics, but a resilient effort from Thompson and the Pistons

articles.title: Los Pistons sobreviven al recital de Paul George (38+5+3) con los Celtics

articles.summary: El fichaje estrella de Boston no evita la derrota ante Detroit (121-113), que recuperó la puntería en el tramo final y sentenció con un parcial de 30-11. Nulo protagonismo de Hugo González
articles.body: La NBA alzó el telón de la nueva temporada con un duelo estelar entre dos de los gallitos de la Conferencia Este, Pistons y Celtics, que acabó decantándose del lado de los de Detroit (121-113), que sobrevivieron al huracán Paul George y a una primera parte muy discreta (45-58), lastrados por su nefasta puntería desde el perímetro (4/18 t3). Mejoraron su acierto tras el descanso y rozaron la perfección al inicio del último para acabar con 15/40 triples y sellar el triunfo con un parcial de 30-11. La remontada de los Pistons fue posible gracias al acierto el tramo final del partido de Duncan Robinson (21 puntos con 5/9 triples), Jalen Duren (22+9) y Javonte Green (19 puntos con 5/8 triples), secundados durante el choque por la estrella del equipo, Cade Cunningham (22+4+8). Enfrente, los Celtics se las prometían muy felices en la primera parte, en pleno éxtasis anotador de Paul George, su fichaje estrella de este verano y que en su debut fue el mejor de su equipo y del partido con 38 puntos (5/9 t2, 7/12 t3 y 7/8 tl), 5 rebotes y 3 asistencias. El alero demostró que si raya a ese nivel es capaz de hacer olvidar a Jaylen Brown. Esa fue la mejor noticia para los de Boston, que constataron que su gran estrella, Jayson Tatum (13+4+11) ha superado la lesión del tendón de Aquiles que sólo le permitió jugar 22 partidos el pasado curso, pero aún necesita rodaje para volver a ser el jugador determinante que era antes de lesionarse. Con él a medio gas, sólo Derrick White (17+1+8) y Payton Pritchard (17+4) arrimaron el hombro junto a Paul George. Los Pistons compitieron de tú a tú hasta el inicio del segundo cuarto (39-39), cuando encajaron un parcial de 6-19 hasta el descanso liderado por el propio Paul George, secundado por Hauser y Pritchard (45-58). Cade Cunningham y Jalen Duren se pusieron las pilas en la reanudación y permitieron a los de Detroit volver a meterse en el partido y llegar vivos antes del último cuarto (82-88). Y en ese último acto los Celtics colapsaron y los Pistons encarrilaron el triunfo con tres triples y tres tiros libres de Duncan Robinson, dos triples de Devonte Green, un 2+1 de Jalen Duren y una canasta de Cunningham (112-99 a 3.33 del final) para mandar a la lona a los Celtics tras un parcial de 30-11. En la que respecta al español Hugo González, su concurso fue casi testimonial. Estuvo en cancha sólo 10 minutos (seis en el segundo cuarto y cuatro en el tercero), en los que cogió tres rebotes y falló el único triple que intentó. Parecía que con la marcha de Jaylen Brown el exmadridista podría contar con más minutos que la pasada campaña, pero de momento en el primer partido no los tuvo.

articles.title: Jayson Tatum, Celtics on Wrong Side of Shocking Stat in NBA Opening Loss to Cade Cunningham, Pistons
articles.summary: The Boston Celtics did not start the 2026-27 season off on the right foot.
articles.body:
The Boston Celtics did not start the 2026-27 season off on the right foot.

Boston blew a 22-point lead in Tuesday's 121-113 loss to the Detroit Pistons on Tuesday and found itself on the wrong side of a notable stat. Insider Keerthika Uthayakumar pointed out it was the team's biggest blown lead since February 2025, which was all the more notable since it was 38-0 last season when building a lead of 20 or more points.

What's more, the NBA announced Detroit's 22-point comeback marked the largest one on the first day of an NBA season since the play-by-play era started in the 1997-98 campaign:

Final Record Predictions for Every NBA Team 🔮

It seemed like the Celtics were going to cruise to a statement win with Jayson Tatum dishing out assists and Paul George thriving in his first game in a new uniform. George finished with 38 points, five steals, five rebounds and three assists and set a franchise record for points in a debut.

However, it wasn't enough in large part because Detroit unleashed a 23-0 run in the fourth quarter to seize control in front of a raucous home crowd.

Cade Cunningham led the way with 22 points, eight assists and four rebounds, while Ausar Thompson played excellent defense on Tatum.

Boston likely wouldn't have ruined George's incredible performance if Tatum played at his normal level, but he dealt with Thompson hounding him on plenty of shots. The Celtics star finished 6-of-23 from the field and 0-of-7 from deep, although he impacted the game with his passing with 11 assists.

It wasn't enough, and the Celtics ended up blowing a lead in a fashion they didn't do all of last season.

articles.body:
New York spent all summer celebrating the Knicks' first NBA championship since 1973.

With LeBron James and the Philadelphia 76ers in town for their season debuts, the Knicks passed out championship rings and raised a banner in front of an ecstatic Madison Square Garden crowd.

The party started with the Larry O'Brien Trophy sitting at center court, surrounded by the rings, ready to be handed out.

Then the players — led by championship heroes Jalen Brunson, OG Anunoby and Karl-Anthony Towns — were introduced to raucous cheers. They got a look at their rings for the first time.

As the players tried on their new hardware, the Knicks released a video detailing the rings' elaborate craftsmanship. In a world where each new championship ring seeks to outdo the last, the Knicks have made a notable entry.

The rings feature Madison Square Garden, inside and out. The top of the ring raises up to show the structure of the world-famous building. That removable top reveals the stands and the court at MSG underneath.

Once the rings were handed out, it was Brunson's turn to take the mic. He delivered a brief speech before getting down to the business at hand.

"What's up, Knicks fans?" Brunson said. "Most importantly, I want to say thank you guys for not leaving Game 4. We really appreciate it. As much as we won this, we wouldn't have done this without you guys. This is unbelievable. It's really a dream come true.

"I know overall we're excited to get this season going. We're ready to turn the page as a team. But one thing I would like to say: The joy that this city had this summer, we would love to replicate that again. Thank you, guys. Let's raise this banner."

LeBron and the 76ers awaited, and it was time to get down to the business of working on securing another banner for the MSG rafters.

White told OutKick that Engelbert’s response does not resolve his challenge to the league’s eligibility standards, calling on the WNBA to explain how it defines men and women. The dispute centers on White’s and Freedom’s efforts to enter the 2027 WNBA draft after declaring that they identify as women. In an Oct. 16 letter responding to Republican lawmakers, Engelbert stated the league’s position directly. articles.title: Can the Bulls win 30 games this season? How the NBA’s new anti-tanking rules may come into play.
articles.summary: CHICAGO — The Chicago Bulls say they’re committed to both winning and losing the right way. But on the eve of the 2026-27 NBA season, it’s difficult to parse...
articles.body:
CHICAGO — The Chicago Bulls say they're committed to both winning and losing the right way. But on the eve of the 2026-27 NBA season, it's difficult to parse out how that will manifest itself.

That's the thing about a rebuild. Wins and losses start to assume the same value, the same role in a team's progress. So coach Tiago Splitter and executive vice president of basketball operations Bryson Graham are committed to being OK with losing. (Or, if not OK with it, at least to stomach it long enough to develop young players and scoop up a couple of decent draft picks.)

That's fine for an executive. It's harder to understand as a fan, especially the weary, long-traveled masses who traverse the Chicago cold to the United Center or those who navigate cable and streaming packages to watch games from home.

Most modern NBA fans understand the importance of a rebuild. But they also want to see their team win. And for the Bulls this season, it's hard to tell how that commitment to development will translate to their record.

It's never ideal to look to betting sources for guidance, and that's especially true this season as the league adjusts to new anti-tanking rules. BetMGM set the over/under for Bulls wins at 29 1/2 — a notably optimistic outlook for the Bulls, who will be battling with other Eastern Conference also-rans to stay out of the new relegation zone.

Although losing is still an acceptable byproduct of a rebuild, the anti-tanking rules no longer incentivize abysmal records. The bottom three teams in each conference will receive worse draft-lottery odds — equal to those of the ninth- and 10th-seeded teams in the play-in tournament.

The change is intended to improve the quality of competition from lesser teams with lower hopes of making the play-in or playoffs. It should lead to fewer blowouts and more compression in the standings as those teams refuse to roll over and risk relegation.

This complicates competition for the Bulls, who tallied either 39 or 40 wins in each of the three consecutive seasons — 2022-23 through 2024-25 — that they made (and then quickly lost in) the play-in tournament.

Those three play-in seasons, however, were a perfect encapsulation of the type of competition the NBA is trying to root out with the new rules. The Bulls were fixated on competitiveness to get into the play-in tournament, but most of their lower-tier competitors in the East focused on tanking. Thus the Bulls padded their way to 39- and 40-win seasons by beating up lottery-bound teams that were happy to absorb the drubbings in exchange for better draft odds.

Last season the Bulls win total dropped to 31, mostly because of the purposeful nose dive taken after half the roster was traded at the February deadline.

This season's roster is more purposefully constructed than that post-deadline team, and the additions of veterans such as Norman Powell and Nic Claxton should provide a buoying effect. But the road to a similar win total is much more difficult.

The Brooklyn Nets and Milwaukee Bucks figure to serve as the East's punching bags, but the Bulls won't get any guaranteed wins against teams like the Charlotte Hornets, Washington Wizards, Atlanta Hawks or Orlando Magic.

The season opens with a demanding three-week gauntlet that includes two games apiece against the Boston Celtics, New York Knicks and Philadelphia 76ers, in addition to games against the San Antonio Spurs and Toronto Raptors. Claxton's ongoing absence heightens the difficulty of the opening stretch. The Bulls will have to rack up wins on the margins this season — a harder feat when the margins have been so greatly diminished.

This might seem pessimistic. But in reality, it's a sign of positive growth for a Bulls team that could be on the rise in a short time.

This season should produce an intriguing "if, then" situation for the Bulls. A season with 30-plus wins would happen only if they see a major leap in growth from either Caleb Wilson or Matas Buzelis. While players such as Powell and Claxton should provide consistency, those two young players are the key variables by which the Bulls can explode upward. An ahead-of-schedule ascent from either would be welcomed by the Bulls, which would reset the timeline of the rebuild.

It's likelier that Buzelis and Wilson will take the expected, appropriate steps forward (and, at times, backward) in their progression this season. Those steps, if made, would be enough to build for the future.

After so many seasons of play-in tournament tunnel vision, it's difficult to reframe a team's focus to this new reality of mid-tier competition. Yet that paradigm shift is essential if the Bulls ever want to break out of the middle of the East and regain their footing as a true conference contender.

Change is for the better in Chicago. But first it will be hard — and hard-fought.

NEW ORLEANS (AP) — The New Orleans Pelicans have exercised a fourth-year option on third-year center Yves Missi, as well as third-year options on both of their 2025 first-round draft picks: guard Jeremiah Fears and forward Derik Queen.

The moves, announced Tuesday, were expected as Missi is the club's projected starting center this season, while both Fears and Queen produced while receiving ample playing time as rookies in the team's first season with Joe Dumars serving as executive vice president of basketball operations.

Missi, drafted 21st overall out of Baylor in the 2024, has appeared in 139 games with 81 starts, averaging 7.5 points, 7.1 rebounds and 1.4 blocks in 23.4 minutes per game.

Fears, drafted seventh overall out of Oklahoma in 2025, played in all 82 games games as a rookie with 49 starts.

Named to the NBA's All-Rookie second team, Fears scored in double-figures 59 times, including 17 games with 20 or more points. He finished the season with averages of 14.3 points, 3.7 rebounds and 3.4 assists in 25.8 minutes per game.

Queen, drafted 13th overall out of Maryland in 2025, also was named NBA All-Rookie second team last season after averaging 11.7 points, 7.1 rebounds and 3.7 assists in 81 games. He started 48 games and played about 25 minutes per game.

Queen recorded two triple doubles last season, the only rookie with more than one.

The Pelicans open the regular season Wednesday night at home against the Indiana Pacers.

articles.title: Paul George scores 38 points in a losing debut with the Celtics
articles.summary: Paul George looks like he’s still got it.
articles.body:
DETROIT (AP) — Paul George looks like he's still got it.

He scored 38 points — the most by a Boston Celtic in his debut, and the fifth-most by a player in his first game with an NBA franchise — in a 121-113 collapsing defeat Tuesday.

"I'm not a moral victory guy," George said after making 12 of 21 shots, including 7 of 12 3-pointers. "It means nothing."

Maybe not, but the nine-time All-Star was impressive and earned a spot in rarified air.

The NBA scoring record for a debut was set by Kyrie Irving in 2019, when he had 50 with the Brooklyn Nets.

Kiki Vandeweghe had 47 points in his first game with Portland in 1984, Wilt Chamberlain scored 43 points in his NBA debut with Philadelphia in 1959 and Damian Lillard had 39 points in his Milwaukee debut in 2023.

George, in his 17th season, was acquired in a trade with the 76ers last summer in exchange for 2024 NBA Finals MVP Jaylen Brown .

Even though George wasn't celebrating his performance due to the loss, the 36-year-old forward was encouraged by his health.

Injuries — and a 25-game suspension for flunking a drug test — limited him to 37 and 41 games the last two regular seasons with the Sixers.

During training camp with the Celtics, George said his legs felt heavy and winded.

In Game 1 with his fifth team, he didn't know what to respect.

"It's hard to know until the lights come on," George said. "It was a rough camp for me."

He looked smooth in Motown in 31 minutes with five steals, five rebounds and three assists.

"It was a thing to watch," teammate Derrick White said. "He got hot and we tried to find him."

The Celtics found George early in the third quarter, leading to him making three 3-pointers in less than a minute to put them ahead 72-50.

Boston then became the fifth team in 30 seasons to lose a season-opening game after leading by 22 points allowed Detroit to earn the biggest comeback win in a league opener since 1997.

"If we're in the driver's seat like that, we'll learn how to close out games," George said.

"He was unbelievable," Jayson Tatum said.

The six-time All-Star missed 17 of 23 shots had 13 points and 11 assists. His lack of hustle on defense allowed Javonte Green to take his time for a fifth 3-pointer that gave the Pistons a 13-point lead with 3:33 left that capped a 23-0 run.

George, though, gave the Celtics a lot to like.

"Just his comfort level," reigning NBA Coach of the Year Joe Mazzulla said. "The game found him, he made some great reads throughout the game. It was good. He was able to find advantages for himself and others, we just have to continue that.

articles.title: Paul George Says He's Getting His 'Pop Back' After Dropping 38 Points in Celtics Debut vs. Pistons
articles.summary: Paul George had two seasons to forget with the Philadelphia 76ers, but he looked more like the star he once was in his debut with the Boston Celtics on Tuesday.
articles.body:
Paul George had two seasons to forget with the Philadelphia 76ers, but he looked more like the star he once was in his debut with the Boston Celtics on Tuesday.

In a loss to the Detroit Pistons, the veteran forward posted 38 points and five steals. After the game, he said he's starting to feel more like himself as he adjusts to his new team.

"Getting back into the swing of things. Playing again. I thought, really, the camp, legs were just heavy," he told reporters . "I was winded a lot of times, so it was taking away the ability to kind of do things when I just felt a little heavy and sluggish. But I'm getting my wind back. I'm getting my legs back. I feel like I'm getting my pop back, and so that was kind of the difference maker."

Despite his outstanding play on Tuesday, George said he had a "rough" training camp. It certainly didn't seem that way once he stepped onto the court.

"It's hard to know until the lights come on," George said . "It was a rough camp for me."

George played just 41 games in his first year with the Sixers before playing just 37 games a season ago. He struggled to stay on the floor consistently, which prevented him from ever getting into much of a rhythm with his teammates.

While George had a positive start to his first season in Boston, the Celtics blew a 22-point lead against the Pistons and clearly have some figuring out to do.

"I'm not a moral victory guy," George said. "It means nothing."

articles.title: Inside LeBron James and Savannah’s Los Angeles home: The NBA superstar and his wife give fans a rare glimpse into their private world beyond basketball and fame
articles.summary: LeBron James makes his regular-season debut for the Philadelphia 76ers against the Knicks in New York.
articles.body: LeBron James makes his regular-season debut for the Philadelphia 76ers against the Knicks in New York. The four-time champion arrives after a video tour of the Los Angeles home James shares with wife Savannah, released by Vogue on Tuesday as part of its Objects of Affection series. It opens with a hyperbaric chamber used for postgame recovery. Four title trophies, a Basquiat painting and a LeBron James Edition Mercedes-Maybach follow. James also talks about sleep, media scrutiny and the lessons sport has delivered, all ahead of a first game in a new uniform.LeBron James and Savannah open the doors to their Los Angeles home in a house tourThe first stop is a Vitaeris hyperbaric chamber, and James opens the tour with a joke about it: “This one has been in the family for a long time.” Savannah is not a fan. “It’s a little bit too small and claustrophobic for my wife,” James said, which leaves the chamber to James alone.“My a** go to sleep when I get in there,” James said. “I don’t want to talk to nobody, see nobody, hear from nobody.” For a player about to start a season with a new team, a sealed pod and a lot of sleep sounds like a sensible plan.The mantel adds career context. Four NBA championship trophies sit there, the first from 2012 with the Miami Heat. Leaving Cleveland for Miami brought heavy media scrutiny at the time, and James looked back on the payoff in plain terms: “When you put in work and you get the reward, it was definitely gratifying.” Another line from the tour fits a debut night in a new city. “Sports have taught me so much about life.”What else did James show in the Vogue home tour?James pulls out a Louis Vuitton jean jacket with no obvious label, and Savannah explains the idea behind it. “We love a quiet luxury moment,” she said, before showing her “not-so-quiet” Ugg x Palace slides. James adds, “We like stuff that feels good and looks good on us.”The home also holds a Jean-Michel Basquiat piece called “Minor Success.” James describes it as one of the first works where the late artist began drawing crowns.Recovery shows up again at the cold plunge. James calls it “one of the best places in the house.” Savannah does not agree with that. “It’s too cold,” she said, and added that James can stay in the longest.The kitchen is where the tour turns lighter. A “Dessert Row” holds rainbow confetti mini-cakes, brownies, donuts and cookies. When James points to a chocolate cake, the joke is easy: “You need a Willy Wonka golden ticket for that.” Savannah says the biggest offender on the row is her husband, who eats chocolate-chip cookies, chocolate cake and ice cream every day.The Mercedes-Maybach S 680 is a LeBron James Edition, one of two. articles.title: Knicks raise NBA championship banner, hand out elaborate rings complete with a miniature Madison Square Garden
articles.summary: With LeBron James and the Philadelphia 76ers in town for their season debuts, the Knicks passed out championship rings and raised a banner in front of an ecs...
articles.body:
New York spent all summer celebrating the Knicks' first NBA championship since 1973.

With LeBron James and the Philadelphia 76ers in town for their season debuts , the Knicks passed out championship rings and raised a banner in front of an ecstatic Madison Square Garden crowd. Unfortunately for the Knicks and their fans, the 76ers spoiled the party with a 106-100 win .

The party started with the Larry O'Brien Trophy sitting at center court, surrounded by the rings, ready to be handed out.

Then the players — led by championship heroes Jalen Brunson, OG Anunoby and Karl-Anthony Towns — were introduced to raucous cheers. They got a look at their rings for the first time.

As the players tried on their new hardware, the Knicks released a video detailing the rings' elaborate craftsmanship. In a world where each new championship ring seeks to outdo the last, the Knicks have made a notable entry.

The rings feature Madison Square Garden, inside and out. The top of the ring rises up to show the structure of the world-famous building. That removable top reveals the stands and the court at MSG underneath.

Once the rings were handed out, it was Brunson's turn to take the mic. He delivered a brief speech before getting down to the business at hand.

"What's up, Knicks fans?" Brunson said. "Most importantly, I want to say thank you guys for not leaving Game 4. We really appreciate it. As much as we won this, we wouldn't have done this without you guys. This is unbelievable. It's really a dream come true.

"I know overall we're excited to get this season going. We're ready to turn the page as a team. But one thing I would like to say: The joy that this city had this summer, we would love to replicate that again. Thank you, guys. Let's raise this banner."

LeBron and the 76ers awaited, and it was time to get down to the business of working on securing another banner for the MSG rafters. That quest is off to an 0-1 start and will continue with a trip to visit the rival Boston Celtics on Friday.

The San Antonio Spurs and Oklahoma City Thunder have quickly become one of the biggest rivalries in the NBA, and it didn't take long for things to get chippy between the two sides on Tuesday.

The Spurs and Thunder met in the Western Conference Finals last season, and the intense series went to seven games before San Antonio knocked out the defending champs en route to its first Finals appearance since 2014.

The two Western Conference powerhouses got to know each other well during that series, and clearly, the tension has been carried into the new season.

Along with the rivalry between the Spurs and Thunder, there has been an unspoken rivalry between Wembanyama and Holmgren throughout their career. Neither has ever taken a direct shot at the other, but Wembanyama has shaded Holmgren a few times in the past.

"At least from a basketball standpoint, there's no comparison between us," Wembanyama said of Holmgren last December.

The personal rivalry between the two started well before their NBA careers, but it has been an interesting storyline in the Spurs vs. Thunder rivalry.

While there were plenty of changes around the NBA this offseason, San Antonio and Oklahoma City remain two of the top contenders to win it all. It wouldn't be a surprise to see those two meet in the Western Conference Finals again this year.

Until then, they'll battle it out in the regular season.

articles.title: The Knicks raised a banner to the MSG rafters. Then LeBron James and the 76ers brought them back to earth
articles.summary: The Knicks raised their first banner in 53 years at MSG, but LeBron James and the 76ers stole the spotlight with a 106-100 win on opening night.
articles.body: The rafters themselves are nothing special, merely a useful space to house lighting and air conditioning. They are dinged up and dingy, fortunate to constantly bask in a golden hue that covers up their imperfections. But to get raised up into them, to hang around the edges like a beautiful curtain, is to achieve an honor reserved for only the luckiest of lucky. Madison Square Garden serves as a lot of things. It is a concert hall and a hockey rink. Bull riders take over its confines once a year. So do monster trucks. And on the rarest of occasions, for very special brides, people celebrate their weddings here. Above all else, though, it bills itself as a basketball court, the epicenter of a basketball city whose playgrounds have birthed legends, some whose skills went worldwide and others whose lore lived only in their neighborhood parks. On Tuesday night, the Garden rafters welcomed the only banner that matters. Fittingly, it took its time to arrive at its new home. Attached to two pulleys, it meandered its way from the ground to just above the center-court scoreboard, casually and methodically rising above the court floor before finally parking itself to the left of the M in Madison Square Garden. A piece of fabric that needed 53 years to stitch together, after all, shouldn’t be rushed through its moment of glory. The last time Knicks fans gathered here, they stood around in stupefied delirium, having witnessed their team come back from 29 down to win Game 4 of the NBA Finals against the San Antonio Spurs. This was just delirium. Along the midtown streets, fans showed out in their jerseys and championship gear, some simple and plenty bedazzled. A marketing genius drove a bus with a glass side around the block of the Garden, declaring that fans should snap a picture of the trophy housed inside (the bus sported Abu Dhabi Tourism logos, so probably not), while folks headed to the turnstiles, unbothered by what Forbes said was the highest get-in price for an NBA opener in league history. With the usual suspects – Mariska Hargitay and Spike Lee – taking their courtside seats along with Roger Goodell and Jon Bon Jovi, the Garden faithful filled the place before the 6:30 p.m. ceremony. They paid proper homage to the old stars there to welcome the new ones to their championship club – Walt Frazier, maestro of the 1973 championship, handed out the rings – but saved their bedlam for their more recent heroes. OG Anunoby, he of the “hand of God” putback in Game 4, earned a raucous ovation, as did Josh Hart, Mikal Bridges and Karl-Anthony Towns. But no one brought the house down quite like Jalen Brunson. The Knicks captain leaned into his new comedic chops, honed on a stint hosting “Saturday Night Live,” and thanked the crowd for sticking around for Game 4. He then hit the right notes, saying that as much as he loved the good will he felt this summer, he’d like to “replicate that again this year.” “Let’s raise a championship,” he finished as the banner headed upwards. Of course, nowhere is glory more fleeting than in sports. Banners may last forever, but success has a very short shelf life. Before the glitter from the Knicks’ meat-hook sized rings stopped shimmering, the NBA nudged everyone along to the new season. In a purposeful confluence of brilliant scheduling, marketing and the business of basketball, the league arranged it so that the kings of New York would have their on-court coronation on the same night they welcomed the king to their court. LeBron James, 41 and in search of a team that could help him write the final championship chapter of his career, debuted his fourth NBA jersey, suiting up for the 76ers. Booed upon introduction and welcomed with chants of “We didn’t want you” - referencing James’ admitting he considered New York before they won the title - James and the Philadelphia 76ers left with the final word in a 106-100 victory. “It’s encouraging,” 76ers head coach Nick Nurse said “I think the intent of what everybody has been doing is right. I’m really happy to come here and get a win. They’re a hell of a team, and when I wake up tomorrow, I’ll probably forget about it.” New York might not, at least not so quickly. As the Sixers absorbed punch after punch and refused to fold, reality returned with at least a whimper, if not a thud. New York fans quickly shed their joy, exchanging it for exasperation. They screeched their aggravation at officials and implored, more than cajoled, their team with “C’mon New York.” It is ridiculous to suggest that the first game in an 82-game slog could be a must-win, but in Philly, where dire usually comes with a extra heap of desperate, it was pretty close. Reeling from the end of their quarterback’s season and the unofficial end to the Eagles’ hopes, the city is about at its limit. The hottest topics waffle between Nick Sirianni’s job security and the treatment of Jalen Hurts’ blood clots, none exactly harbingers of good news. The Flyers were done before they started and the Phillies long gone. Into the abyss walks the most unsuspecting of would-be heroes. No one in the city has turned to the Sixers for salvation for years, accustomed to a process that never proceeded. Philly hasn’t so much tasted the Eastern Conference finals since 2001, marching coaches through a revolving door as it refused to fix what truly ailed the franchise. But this offseason, the owners finally made moves, bringing in Bob Myers, the architect of Golden State’s brilliance, and Mike Gansey. Together, the two reworked Philly’s fortunes, pulling off a move for Jaylen Brown from the Celtics, and then using that – along with the moxie of Tyrese Maxey – to lure James to, of all places, Philly. It crafted a fever dream for Philly, a team built not just to take baby steps toward success, but to sprint there. The first effort was hardly a work of art. The Sixers’ starting five hit just 29 of their 71 field goals, looking regularly like exactly what they are – a team still learning how to connect all of their disparate parts. But no one came here expecting to solve all the riddles at once. “Obviously this is a marathon,” James said. “But on day one, day six, seven, whatever, the experience that we have we want it to translate to wins and more of a culture – a championship culture.” Perhaps one that ends with a banner celebration all their own.

articles.title: Thunder Dominate Spurs in Opener, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Wemby, SGA, Chet, Top Players
articles.summary: There was no repeat of the Western Conference Finals on the opening night of the 2026-27 NBA season.
articles.body:
There was no repeat of the Western Conference Finals on the opening night of the 2026-27 NBA season.

The Oklahoma City Thunder got some revenge on the San Antonio Spurs with a 116-104 victory in Tuesday's highly anticipated showdown at Frost Bank Center. And if the first game was any indication, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander could be well on his way to a third straight MVP.

SGA was the best player on the floor as he unleashed his normal combination of midrange jumpers and silky smooth moves, while Victor Wembanyama couldn't keep pace as he struggled with his own shot (1-of-13) against OKC's stifling defense.

Jared McCain provided support with six threes off the bench, which helped the Thunder overcome strong showings from Stephon Castle, De'Aaron Fox and Dylan Harper.

The Spurs fell short in the NBA Finals, but they entered this season with momentum in the matchup of heavyweights with the Thunder after winning Game 7 of the Western Conference Finals on the road. It would be anything but shocking if these two teams faced each other on that stage again, this was a chance for both sides to make an early statement.

And the tension was on display right from the start.

It boiled over some in the second quarter when things got heated after Fox threw Chet Holmgren to the ground. The teams had to be separated, and the end result was a flagrant foul for Fox, a technical for Wembanyama and technicals for all three Williams on the Thunder (Jaylin, Jalen and Kenrich).

For as amusing as the trio of Williams technicals was, the Spurs fans likely took little joy from the rest of the first half.

Oklahoma City jumped out to a commanding 21-point lead by intermission with McCain and Alex Caruso draining threes off the bench, the defense frustrating Wembanyama, and Gilgeous-Alexander taking over for extended stretches.

SGA is nearly impossible to stop when he attacks the lane, but he also mixed in multiple triples and facilitated to Holmgren when interior defenders collapsed on his penetration. With Wembanyama missing all of his field-goal attempts in the first half on the other end, the Thunder were in full control behind their star advantage.

To San Antonio's credit, it battled back in the third quarter and cut the deficit to single digits with Fox and Castle picking up the scoring slack for Wembanyama, who didn't make his first field goal until his 13th attempt.

The big man still impacted the game by swatting shots and getting to the free-throw line, but Gilgeous-Alexander had an answer seemingly every time the Spurs made a run. That kept the Thunder up 13 heading to the fourth after a response that included rookie Aday Mara blocking Wembanyama on one end and finishing a dunk on the other.

It was more of the same in the fourth quarter, as the Spurs went on an early run when Gilgeous-Alexander was on the bench just for the point guard to push the lead back to double digits when he returned to the floor.

It wasn't a one-man show, as McCain drilled a critical three-pointer, Holmgren blocked a shot at the rim and Caruso bothered San Antonio's perimeter players with his hounding defense down the stretch.

With the role players contributing and SGA torching Spurs defenders, OKC was in full control by the final minutes and will have a chance to build some early season momentum when it faces another Western Conference contender in the Denver Nuggets on Thursday.

articles.title: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Thunder shut down Victor Wembanyama to roll past Spurs on opening night
articles.summary: Victor Wembanyama opened the game by missing his first 12 shots in what was the worst shooting start to any contest in his career.
articles.body: The NBA's reigning two-time MVP is picking up right where he left off. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander led the Oklahoma City Thunder to a 116-104 win over Victor Wembanyama and the San Antonio Spurs at the Frost Bank Center on Tuesday night to kick off the 2026-27 NBA season. Gilgeous-Alexander looked as confident as ever coming out of the offseason and dropped 32 points with 5 rebounds and 4 assists. The Thunder pretty easily shut down Wembanyama, too. He had just 12 points and 13 rebounds, and had only a single made field goal on the night. Wembanyama bolted off the court as soon as the final buzzer sounded."We're just happy to be back," Gilgeous-Alexander said on NBC after the win. "The NBA's back. It's a longer summer when you don't win, and we felt that this summer. We're just happy to be back. "[It's] one of 82. This doesn't prove anything, this doesn't mean anything. … We took a step in the right direction."Thunder run away in heated first halfThe rivalry between the Thunder and Spurs heated up almost instantly on Tuesday night. After a contentious stretch early, Spurs guard De'Aaron Fox suddenly grabbed Thunder star Chet Holmgren by the hip and slammed him down as they were jostling for position in the paint. Holmgren, the 7-foot-1 center, is almost a full foot taller than Fox. That, of course, led to a pretty big scuffle in the paint. In the end, Wembanyama, Jalen Williams, Jaylin Williams and Kenrich Williams all received technical fouls for their actions. Fox was hit with a flagrant, too. Flagrant foul 1 on De’Aaron Fox for throwing Chet Holmgren to the ground.Victor Wembanyama, Jaylin Williams, Jalen Williams, and Kenrich Williams all pick up technical fouls after the Spurs and Thunder get into a scuffle in the second quarter of tonight’s season opener.…— Brett Siegel (@BrettSiegelNBA) October 21, 2026 But that sparked a huge run for the Thunder. They broke the game open with a quick 9-0 run after the altercation and ended up pushing it to 22-3 to take a 26-point lead at its peak. Gilgeous-Alexander dropped 16 points in the first half, and the Thunder took a 21-point lead into the break. They had 11 different players score, and went an impressive 10 of 14 from the 3-point line.Wembanyama, meanwhile, struggled offensively. While he had three blocks in the first 24 minutes, he went a rough 0 of 7 from the field. The Spurs opened the second half about as good as they could have and cut the game back to single digits after a 14-3 run. But it didn't last long, thanks in part to a huge sequence from Thunder rookie Aday Mara. The big man stuffed Wembanyama at the rim and then threw down his own lob at the other end just moments later.Aday Mara MAKING PLAYS in his first NBA game 🔥Big-time swat at the rim.Two-hand alley-oop slam.The Thunder lead in Q3! pic.twitter.com/YJpmoBAm8J— NBA (@NBA) October 21, 2026 Wembanyama finally got his first bucket of the night to fall right at the buzzer of the third quarter on a reverse slam. He had missed his first 12 shots of the night, which is the worst shooting start in any game of his career. But the dunk cut the deficit to 13 points and kept the Spurs within striking distance. In the end, though, the Spurs just couldn't recover from their first-half struggles. The Thunder expertly survived one last push in the fourth to cruise to the 12-point win.Stephon Castle led the Spurs with 24 points and seven rebounds. Dylan Harper added 18 points, and Fox finished with 14 points and seven rebounds.Jared McCain added 20 points off the bench for the Thunder to go with Gilgeous-Alexander's night. McCain made a career-high six 3-pointers, too. Holmgren finished with 14 points and seven rebounds.While it's only the first night of the regular season, and these two teams will meet again plenty of times over the next several months, the Thunder clearly were itching for revenge after last season's loss in the Western Conference finals. This rivalry is, clearly, alive and well.

articles.title: New-look 76ers flash glimpses of what could be against defending champion Knicks
articles.summary: With new additions Jaylen Brown and LeBron James in tow, Philadelphia turned it on down the stretch and made some noise on opening night.
articles.body:
NEW YORK — The thing to remember is, the New York Knicks didn't want to leave VJ Edgecombe all by himself.

Like, all things being equal, you'd imagine they'd prefer to cover a player who averaged 16 points per game and converted 61% of his point-blank tries as a rookie for the Philadelphia 76ers, and has the kind of rocket propulsion in his calves that enable him to elevate and detonate above defenders at the rim. That's not the kind of guy you typically like to leave open.

It's just that, well, Tyrese Maxey had the ball at the start of the play, and he's an All-NBA lightning bolt who looked like the best player on the floor for the bulk of Tuesday's season-opening contest at Madison Square Garden. So when he dribbled off a high ball screen late in the fourth quarter, having watched him slice and dice his way through their defense on multiple occasions, the Knicks decided to blitz him to try to force the ball out of his hands.

That strategy worked well for the Knicks during their sweep of the Sixers in the second round last spring , as they marauded their way through the Eastern Conference en route to the NBA title that they spent the early portion of Tuesday evening celebrating. This time, though, Maxey was ready for it, slipping the ball through the blitz to the now-healthy and noticeably slimmer Joel Embiid, who'd set the ball screen and was ready to take the feed from Maxey at the foul line and keep the play extended.

Embiid, you might recall, was the Most Valuable Player of the whole stinkin' league a few seasons ago and can still look like one of the most dominant offensive players in the world when he's right. The Knicks didn't want to let him run rampant either; they'd really prefer to have someone help out the low man as he steps up to stop the ball, pinching in from the corners to protect the paint.

The thing is, though, that after Philadelphia's stunning summertime makeover, one of those corners was occupied by Jaylen Brown, who averaged 28.7 points per game last season. The other was occupied by LeBron James, who, as you might have heard, is the leading scorer in the history of the sport.

You don't want to leave either of those guys alone, either. And so …

"If I can score like that the whole game," a smiling Edgecombe told reporters after the contest, "I'm perfectly fine with that."

You'd suspect the rest of the Sixers will be, too.

Those interior buckets helped keep New York at arm's length late in the fourth quarter Tuesday — a night the Knicks began with a coronation , but ended with the bitter taste of a 106-100 defeat to their Atlantic Division rivals.

"That's what we wanted to do — be a little spoiler," said Brown, who headed to Philadelphia in a blockbuster trade with the Boston Celtics this summer and finished with 19 points, 8 rebounds and 6 assists in his maiden voyage as a Sixer. "Obviously, what the Knicks accomplished is great. But it's a new season, new year."

And the 76ers are a new team. Brown and James (14 points, 9 rebounds, 7 assists) bring a combination of offensive firepower, defensive versatility and hard-earned experience at the highest level to a franchise that hasn't advanced past the second round of the playoffs since 2001. A pair of lower-wattage newcomers, guards Anfernee Simons and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, played pivotal roles Tuesday, combining to knock down five 3-pointers to help Philly's offense get unstuck and put the defending champs on their heels.

"Those were incredibly huge tonight," Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said. "I thought we were generating a bunch of wide-open 3s and just nobody could throw one in. And those guys kind of broke through on that and moved the scoreboard for us."

Both teams struggled moving the scoreboard in the early going. A Knicks team perhaps a bit emotionally spent from receiving their championship rings and watching a banner hoisted to the rafters at Madison Square Garden shot just 37% from the field in the first quarter. A Philly squad still very much in the getting-to-know-you phase wasn't much better, shooting just 40.9% in the opening frame. The two teams combined to miss 15 of their first 19 3-point tries, trading stagnant possessions, fouls and free throws in a slog of an affair.

After entering halftime trailing by four, though, the Sixers started to kick into gear in the third. They made only 12 field goals in 27 tries, but all 12 were assisted — evidence that, despite many pundits' "there's only one ball" doom-saying, Philly's players were committed to sharing the wealth.

"We're getting into some actions," Nurse said. "We make the next read, and the guys are just trying to read where the ball's supposed to go. I think we're just making good decisions, and I think you could throw that around to just about everybody. Obviously, I thought Joel made some huge ones, LeBron made some big ones, but I think Tyrese made a couple, as well. So, again, just keep trying to make the right play."

They showed that commitment on the other end, too. The Sixers held New York to 18 points on 5-for-21 shooting in the third quarter, which they closed with a 14-2 run capped by a buzzer-beating triple by Brown that sent Philly into the fourth up by seven; they would hold the lead throughout the fourth, holding Jalen Brunson, Karl-Anthony Towns and Co. at bay.

"That third quarter, that just gives you an outlook on what we can become," Embiid said.

The Sixers limited the champs to just 14 points in the paint after intermission. For the game, they forced 14 Knicks turnovers and turned them into 22 points, with a number of them coming in the blink of an eye. They scored 1.8 points per play in transition on Tuesday and an absurd 2.2 points per play off steals, according to Cleaning the Glass — a level of offensive efficiency after a change of possession that can help you overcome a shaky shooting night.

They rotated on a string, closed out hard to shooters and forced drivers to attack Embiid, who was hobbled and largely immobile when these two teams squared off in the playoffs, but who looked notably more nimble Tuesday. He blocked three shots, altered a number of others and came away with a pair of steals — an impressive and encouraging performance for a player who needs to be excellent defensively for Philly to get where it wants to go and who wasn't shy about saying Tuesday he feels like he'll be returning to All-Defensive form this season.

"I told Tyrese after the game: We've been going against these guys for the last couple of years, and it felt — tonight felt a little different than the past," Embiid said.

"We have the talent," Embiid said. "I just think we have more focus in everything we do. Just be locked in every single possession. Defensively, I think a lot of it falls on me, and I'll put it on me. If I want [to make the] All-Defensive team like past seasons, everything changes. If I can [do that] every single night, which I will, everything changes."

The ceiling could be even higher if Maxey — who scored a game-high 28 points on 9-for-19 shooting with 5 assists — continues to play like the No. 1 option even when surrounded by All-Stars. Just as notable as his relentless pace with the ball in his hands, the seventh-year guard also added three blocks and three steals — the last of which led to a fast-break dunk that gave the Sixers a six-point lead with 1:52 remaining.

"I think our guys were doing pretty good as far as being connected, and whenever Tyrese darts into a lane and steals one, I'm not that surprised, because he's really got a burst of speed to make those kinds of plays," Nurse said. "But yeah — really timely, right? It was really close, really close. It looked like it was going down to the last possession, and all of a sudden, he gets a breakaway layup, I think, to put us up six."

"I had fun — a lot of fun," Maxey said. "This group is very competitive. I've been saying it all training camp. And you saw it tonight, extremely competitive on both ends of the floor. You could tell the guys don't like losing."

You could also tell, though, that the Sixers are much closer to the start of their collective journey than the finish line.

"We'll have some of those moments in the early run of the season," James said. "We're still new to each other. We had a couple of moments where we had some turnovers that was kind of unforced. We had some moments where we had some open looks and we didn't take it. And that will happen early on in the season, as we continue to build, as we continue to build our offensive sets, build our defensive sets. We will have some bumps in the road at times. But I think tonight, when we had those bumps in the road — which a good team will usually do — we were able to use what happened previously and then make the adjustment."

The Sixers are learning and growing, and nowhere near a finished product. But if they can win while they learn and grow, while already showing some glimpses of what that finished product might be, then they might have the makings of something special in the City of Brotherly Love.

"We're not even at the tip of the iceberg in terms of building chemistry, understanding yourself on the floor, understanding our spacing," Brown said. "Like, we're still at the very early stages of what we could possibly be."

articles.title: Aday Mara debuta en la NBA metiendo en un póster a Wembanyama
articles.standfirst: El pívot español firmó la jugada defensiva del partido
articles.summary: El pívot español firmó la jugada defensiva del partido
articles.body: La Conferencia Oeste arrancó en la NBA con la redición del duelo que ambos equipos protagonizaron buscando un lugar en las Finales y que finalmente encontró San Antonio. En esta ocasión, los Thunder dieron el primer golpe en la mesa con su triunfo en el Frost Bank Center. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander volvió a ser el líder de un equipo que mantiene intactas sus ilusiones de repetir título de campeón. El canadiense fue el termómetro del partido con 32 puntos, especialmente en la segunda mitad, cuando el partido se estaba decidiendo. En el otro lado, el arranque de temporada de Victor Wembanyama se diluyó en un horrible 1 de 13 en tiros, que le dio 12 puntos y 13 rebotes. Pero sobre todo se vio involucrado en el póster del partido (y seguro que uno de los mejores de la temporada) en el que le metió un rookie español que jamás olvidará su debut en la NBA. Tardó poco en producirse el estreno del zaragozano. A 5:39 para el final del primer cuarto, Mara salía en sustitución de Chet Holmgren y 36 segundos más tarde ya era objeto de falta personal por parte de Wemby. Mara falló el primer tiro libre pero anotó el segundo, su primer punto en la NBA. Mara siguió produciendo en su fabulosa puesta en escena en la mejor Liga del mundo. A 3:01 para el final de ese primer cuarto capturó su primer rebote, y a 2:28 llegó su primera asistencia, su destinatario fue Jared McCain (21-26). En su segundo regreso a la pista, a 5:22 para el final del tercer cuatro, firmó la primera de las tres canastas en juego que logró (66-78). Pero la jugada que ya ha dado la vuelta al mundo se produjo a 4:20 para el final del tercer acto. Wembanyama se disponía a culminar un alle-oop con un mate cuando se encontró a Mara que le negó el paso convirtiendo la jugada en una taponazo brutal, Pero lo que fue una defensa sensacional de su aro se convirtió en una contraataque del pívot para finalizar la secuencia con una mate tras un alley-oop (70-84). La mejor carta de presentación de Mara como jugador de la NBA. 'Big Spain', como le llama Kenrich Williams que en pretemporada ya vio que Mara puede estar en el primer o segundo quinteto defensivo de la Liga, acabó el partido en el que jugó 12 minutos con 7 puntos, 3/4 en tiros de dos y 1/2 en tiros libres, dos rebotes, una asistencia y un tapón. Su +/- fue de +9, pero su su impacto en el partido fue mucho mayor. Mara brilló en su debut en el que los Thunder empezaron a construir su venganza contras los Spurs. Son los dos máximos favoritos en el Oeste y su batalla acaba de comenzar. OKC se llevó el primer asalto y Aday Mara ya le conocen en la NBA.

articles.title: LeBron James' Philadelphia 76ers knock off champion New York Knicks in sensational road victory to open NBA season
articles.summary: The Philadelphia 76ers beat the New York Knicks side 106-100 at Madison Square Garden in LeBron James' debut with his new team; James recorded 14 points, nine rebounds and six assists to complement standout performer Tyrese Maxey's 28-point haul
articles.body:
James began his NBA-record 24th season with 14 points, nine rebounds and six assists, while Tyrese Maxey scored 28 points and James' fellow Sixers debutant Jaylen Brown had 19 points, eight rebounds and six assists in his first game since being acquired from Boston.

Jalen Brunson scored 21 points but the NBA Finals MVP shot just 6 for 19 from the field.

Brunson told fans inside Madison Square Garden in a pregame ceremony when the Knicks raised their NBA championship banner and received their rings that: "The joy that this city had this summer, we would love to replicate that again."

Maybe they can, but they will have to play a lot better than they did Tuesday in shooting 37 per cent overall and 33.3 per cent on 3s. Centre Karl-Anthony Towns was the standout, with 19 points and 12 rebounds.

The Knicks dominated the 76ers in a second-round sweep in last season's playoffs, early on during their streak of 13 straight victories as part of a 16-3 finish with the highest point differential in NBA postseason history.

Philadelphia then went out and traded for Brown - the NBA's scoring champion last season - and signed James after the NBA's all-time scoring leader decided to leave the Los Angeles Lakers, setting the 76ers up with the potential to be one of the best teams in the league.

They certainly didn't have a smooth start but played better as the game went on. The Sixers closed the third quarter with an 11-0 run, capped by Brown's second straight 3-pointer that came at the buzzer and gave Philadelphia an 83-76 lead.

Maxey's three-point play early in the fourth made it 87-78. The Knicks cut it to 96-95 when Towns made a 3-pointer, but Joel Embiid answered in kind and the Sixers stayed ahead.

Embiid finished with 13 points, 11 rebounds and six assists.

Brunson, wearing gold sneakers for the occasion, couldn't help the Knicks recover by hitting the type of big shots he did when they repeatedly came back to beat San Antonio in five games for their first championship since 1973.

The festive pregame party gave way to a first half filled with long stretches of fouls and missed shots, not leaving much reason for the cheers to continue. The Knicks went ahead by 10 with one good flurry but it was down to 58-54 at halftime.

While the opening game of the regular season is merely one of 82 that the 76ers will have to play, they could have hardly got off to a better start than defeating the reigning champions on the road at the first time of asking.

LeBron: Blessed to still be at this level

A reflective James spoke post-match of his appreciation for still being involved in a match at the pinnacle of his sport, with the 41-year-old starting his record-extending 24th NBA season:

" I feel a lot better. Still getting my rhythm," James said. "Just a little bit over two weeks with the new squad but I like the way we played.

"I think we played exceptionally well especially defensively. We didn't shoot the ball well but we have capable shooters. We know that. So, a good way to start the season.

"It's about winning. Just try to make plays to win.

"I'm very familiar with every scenario that this game has offered.

"[I feel] Blessed to still be able to play it still at this level and uh blessed to be able to play in this building too."

MVP Gilgeous-Alexander leads Thunder to revenge victory over Spurs

Shai Gilgeous-Alexander had 32 points as the Oklahoma City Thunder opened their season with a 116-104 victory over the San Antonio Spurs, the team that ended their dreams of a title defense last season.

San Antonio star Victor Wembanyama had 12 points but was 1 for 13 from the field. It was his fewest field goals since going 2 for 5 against Minnesota on May 10. Wembanyama's lone field goal came on an alley-oop pass from De'Aaron Fox as time expired in the third quarter. Wembanyama missed his first 12 shots, including having an alley-oop attempt blocked by 7-foot-3 rookie Aday Mara.

Jared McCain added 20 points on 6-for-8 shooting on 3-pointers as Oklahoma City led for all but the opening five minutes of the game.

The Spurs beat the Thunder 111-103 in Oklahoma City in Game 7 of the Western Conference Finals on May 30 in their previous matchup.

Nearly five months apart did not cool this heated rivalry.

Three minutes into the second quarter Fox received a Flagrant Foul 1 for tossing Chet Holmgren to the court after they became entangled in the paint. The body slam led to a huge scrum with Wembanyama and Jaylin Williams having to be separated after pushing each other. Wembanyama, Williams, Jalen Williams and Kenrich Williams each received a technical for the dust up.

Oklahoma City went on a 9-0 run after the scuffle with Jalen and Kenrich Williams accounting for five points. Harrison Barnes' 3-pointer ended the run, but the Thunder responded by scoring 13 straight capped by Cason Wallace's 3-pointer for a 59-33 lead.

Oklahoma City outscored San Antonio 31-16 in the second quarter in taking a 65-44 lead at the half.

The Spurs opened the second half on a 23-9 run to pull within single digits after trailing by 26 in the first half.

Gilgeous-Alexander and McCain stepped up when San Antonio pulled close, combining for 25 points in the second half.
