articles.title: NBA: LeBron James' Philadelphia 76ers beat New York Knicks in the season opener
articles.summary: LeBron James scores 14 points on debut for the Philadelphia 76ers as they defeat champions the New York Knicks on the opening night of the NBA season.
articles.body:
LeBron James scored 14 points on his debut for the Philadelphia 76ers as they defeated champions the New York Knicks on the NBA season's opening night.

The 41-year-old James, entering a record-extending 24th season in the league with his fourth team after his summer move from the LA Lakers, also racked up seven assists as his new side triumphed 106-100.

Tyrese Maxey top-scored with 28 points for the 76ers, while Jaylen Brown, who also made his debut after joining the 76ers from the Boston Celtics in a high profile trade for Paul George, scored 19 points with eight rebounds and six assists.

The Knicks enjoyed title celebrations prior to the match, raising their third title banner to the rafters at Madison Square Garden in the presence of a crowd that included celebrity Knicks fans Ben Stiller and Spike Lee.

The Knicks ended a 53-year title drought with their victory over the San Antonio Spurs in last season's NBA Finals but were unable to open their season with a win as the 76ers held out after taking the lead in the third quarter.

Jalen Brunson led the scoring for the Knicks with 21 points and Karl-Anthony Towns picked up 19 points with 12 rebounds.

"I could be a lot better," James told broadcaster NBC. "Still getting my rhythm, obviously just a little bit over two weeks with the new squad.

"But I like the way we played. I think we played exceptionally well, especially defensively."

In the opening match of the NBA's 81st season, the Detroit Pistons fought back in the second half to win 121-113 against the Boston Celtics.

Cade Cunningham and Jalen Duren added 22 points each and Duncan Robinson scored 15 of his 21 in the fourth quarter as the home side secured their victory with a 23-0 scoring run.

Celtics debutant Paul George scored 38 points for his new side in a match between last season's top two regular-season teams.

In the night's final encounter, back-to-back NBA most valuable player Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored 32 points for the Oklahoma City Thunder as they completed a 116-104 win over the San Antonio Spurs.

Stephon Castle top-scored for the Spurs with 24 points but his side were unable to match the form that saw them put out defending champions Thunder in last season's Western Conference finals.

Victor Wembanyama made just one basket in 13 attempts for the Spurs but contributed 13 rebounds and six blocked shots and scored 12 points largely thanks to 10 free throws.

"Obviously, this is the team that eliminated us from achieving our goal," Gilgeous-Alexander said.

"But for us, I think it was more like we're just happy to be back. It's a longer summer when you don't win and we felt that this summer."

articles.title: LeBron y los Sixers arruinan la fiesta de los campeones Knicks
articles.standfirst: Los Sixers se presentan en su estreno como serios candidatos al título
articles.summary: Los Sixers se presentan en su estreno como serios candidatos al título
articles.body: La noche en el Madison no pudo ser perfecta. Empezó bien, con la entrega de los anillos a los campeones, una joya innovadora con el escenario del partido en su interior. Siguió genial, con la subida a los cielos del pabellón del 'banner' que dice que los Knicks son los campeones 2025-26. Los aficionados neoyorquinos han tardado 53 años en volver a ver esa ceremonia. Pero a partir de ahí, la pesadilla. Para esta temporada la NBA ha recuperado una de sus mejores rivalidades de siempre. Knicks y Sixers se van a encontrar en el cruce de caminos que lleve a la final de la NBA. Hace décadas ambos equipos mantenían luchas cerradas en el Este por ser uno de los mejores. Pero aquello se perdió con los dos equipos nadando en la mediocridad. Este año esa batalla será muy distinta. Y el primer capítulo tuvo lugar en el estreno de la temporada en el Madison y se lo llevaron los Sixers. Ganaron a los campeones, arruinando su fiesta, pero sobre todo dejaron claro que presentan desde hoy su candidatura al anillo. Philly ha vuelto. Primer partido y nada de dosificaciones en los Sixers. Ni el escenario ni el momento pedían ahorro de esfuerzos. Y claro, minutada para el cinco titular más potente de la Liga: 40 minutos para Maxey, 35 para Brown y Edgecombe, 34 para LeBron y 33 para Embiid. Y sólo cuatro jugadores del banquillo salieron en algún momento, con Caldwell-Pope (26) y Simmons (25) los más utilizados. Maxey lo cogió donde lo dejó el año pasado, siendo el mejor anotador de su equipo con 28 puntos, Brown aportó 19 y James firmó un buen debut con su nuevo equipo, con 14 puntos, 9 rebotes y 7 asistencias. A sus 41 años sigue teniendo un triple-doble en sus manos. El primer día y los 3,7 millones de dólares que cobra ya están casi amortizados... En los Knicks brillaron Brunson (21), Towns (19) y Hart (14), pero el equipo se quedó en un 37% en tiros de campo, en parte por el 6 de 19 del MVP de las pasadas Finales. Los Knicks tendrán que mejorar su puntería si quieren repetir sensaciones de campeón como prometió Brunson a los aficionados. El tercer cuatro, 19-28, empezó a decantar el partido que hasta ese momento se movía en la igualdad de fuerzas. Al final de la primera mitad, con la tercera falta de Embiid, LeBron ocupó su plaza como '5' en la pista. "Fue una sugerencia mías a los entrenadores. Con tres faltas era peligroso seguir, y pensé que esa era una buena solución", reveló Embiid al final del partido. Eso despeja dudas sobre si LeBron jugará como pívot en muchas fases de la temporada. Lo hará, "Estuvimos jugando con fuego y al final, si Brunson hubiera anotado algunos de los últimos tiros, hubiéranos ganado. Pero algo en mi interior prefería que no fuera así. No se puede jugar con fuego y ganar", analizó con sinceridad el entrenador de los Knicks Mike Brown. Al final de la noche, que comenzó con la gran fiesta de los Knicks, se quedó la sensación de que los Sixers han construído realmente un equipo que puede luchar por ese anillo que vieron repartir. Pero es sólo el primer capítulo, queda todo el camino por recorrer.

articles.title: La WNBA descarta a Enes Kanter y Royce White, dos ex de la NBA, al definirlos como "hombres"
articles.standfirst: "La WNBA acaba de dar el primer paso para definir qué es una mujer en el ámbito deportivo y reconoce que identificarse como mujer no altera la biología humana fundamental"
articles.summary: "La WNBA acaba de dar el primer paso para definir qué es una mujer en el ámbito deportivo y reconoce que identificarse como mujer no altera la biología humana fundamental"
articles.body: Cathy Engelbert, comisionada de la WNBA, informó a legisladores republicanos que los exjugadores de la NBA Enes Kanter Freedom y Royce White no reúnen los requisitos para jugar en la WNBA debido a que "ambos son hombres". Engelbert respondió así a una consulta del Congreso, sin proporcionar la definición de "mujeres" que los legisladores habían solicitado. Los legisladores preguntaron cómo define la WNBA el término "mujeres" conforme al artículo XIII, sección 1(a), de su convenio colectivo, y por qué los dos exjugadores de la NBA fueron considerados no elegibles. "Con respecto a sus preguntas sobre la elegibilidad, sólo las mujeres pueden jugar en la WNBA, y las personas que ustedes mencionan en su carta son, ambos, hombres", escribió Engelbert en su respuesta del 16 de octubre. El documento fue facilitado al medio 'OutKick' por el America First Policy Institute (AFPI), organización que representa a Enes Kanter Freedom. La carta de Engelbert no anunció una nueva norma de elegibilidad ni detalló una política más amplia que regule a las atletas transgénero. Freedom y White habían anunciado su intención de participar en el draft de la WNBA de 2027, afirmando al mismo tiempo que se identifican como mujeres. "Cathy Engelbert no puede definir claramente qué es una mujer, pero está absolutamente segura de que yo soy un hombre. Es decir, ¿qué sentido tiene eso? ¿Quién decide? ¿Quién tiene la autoridad para determinar si alguien es mujer? Si la WNBA todavía está analizando estas cuestiones, ¿cómo puede su comisionada estar tan segura sobre mi elegibilidad sin explicar los criterios que está aplicando?", declaró Enes Kanter Freedom a 'OutKick'. Al preguntársele si consideraba que Engelbert había utilizado un género incorrecto al referirse a él en su carta al Congreso, Freedom respondió: "Sí, al 100 %... Sólo quiero que ella respete mi identidad, porque les digo que me identifico como mujer". Enes Kanter Freedom subrayó que "esto va más allá de una sola jugadora de baloncesto. Es decir, ¿quién determina la identidad de alguien? ¿La propia persona, la comisionada, un profesional médico, un comité o un grupo de trabajo? ¿Y quién determina la elegibilidad para competir en la categoría femenina? Son decisiones que pueden ser diferentes, pero la WNBA debe explicar dónde traza la línea". La carta daba respuesta a una consulta realizada el 17 de septiembre por el congresista republicano por Indiana, Marlin Stutzman, junto con otros cuatro republicanos de la Cámara de Representantes, acerca de los criterios de elegibilidad, la seguridad de las jugadoras y los enfrentamientos con los aficionados. "La WNBA acaba de dar el primer paso para definir qué es una mujer en el ámbito deportivo. Al clasificar claramente a Enes Kanter Freedom y a Royce White como hombres, han reconocido que identificarse como mujer no altera la biología humana fundamental", señaló Stutzman en un comunicado.

articles.title: Thunder remind Spurs of their championship pedigree in statement-making opening win
articles.summary: The Thunder smothered Victor Wembanyama and overwhelmed the Spurs, offering an early reminder of why their championship-tested core remains a force to be rec...
articles.body:
SAN ANTONIO — It's somewhat ironic that the Oklahoma City Thunder's greatest display of strength came as their 7-foot center was flung to the ground by a man nearly a foot shorter, but rivalries are an inexact science.

Three minutes into the second quarter, with Oklahoma City firing on all cylinders and the San Antonio Spurs seemingly unable to keep pace, the hosts' discontent reached its apex. De'Aaron Fox wrapped up Chet Holmgren and dragged him to the floor, drawing a Flagrant 1. The ensuing scuffle earned technical fouls for all three of the Thunder's Williamses: Jalen, Jaylin and Enrich. Fox and Victor Wembanyama, at the heart of the Spurs' frustrations, had been wearing them openly all night.

Wembanyama, who at that time had not recorded a made field goal, was being blitzed, bumped and bruised by Thunder hands and feet. Fox was visibly having a difficult time adjusting to a new lineup in a prime-time showing, logging the lowest usage of his career and finishing with an involvement near-identical to his rookie season .

Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Basketball league for the 2026-27 NBA season

At the heart of it, however, was a stubborn, veteran, championship group that looked more prepared, more ready for the moment. A stubborn, veteran, championship group that didn't forget the high-fives, hugs and hurrahs from their sworn enemy on their home turf. A reminder that the Thunder, at full strength — regardless of departing pieces — are a force to be reckoned with.

"I think our collective understanding of the opponent evolves over time," head coach Mark Daigneault said following the 116-104 win . "Last year was the first year that San Antonio was on the scene the way they were — they had young players that were highly impactful. So it takes time to learn the opponent. We try to take lessons from last season, we played them a lot."

Five months ago, two Western Conference titans clawed, scratched and fought over a grueling, exhilarating seven-game series — with each contest a back-and-forth mental game of pickleball. Because of the few degrees of separation between Oklahoma City and San Antonio, the process of adapting and adjusting is a never-ending affair. Even in late October, while the emotions that come with a rematch feed the flames, it's challenging to get a true tactical read on the opponent at the other end of the rope.

But the Spurs' introduction of their three-guard lineup, a shift from what the Thunder were used to, wasn't just another wrench thrown into the mix. Such a stylistic and ideological move comes with its own challenges.

How Oklahoma City reacted, a combination of Daigneault's genius and the roster's versatility, proved vital. The Thunder decided to experiment with various defensive principles stemming from their 2-3 zone. Man-to-man shading remained a constant with cross-matching being introduced as well, putting a player like Isaiah Hartenstein on Stephon Castle and trusting the rotations behind if necessary. They swarmed when necessary and packed the paint, shortening from the corners and essentially forcing the Spurs to take a high number of corner looks. (The Thunder have won three of the last four meetings when allowing 90th-percentile or higher corner 3 rates.) San Antonio missed 27 of their 37 perimeter attempts, which might be an anomaly for a group that finished league average in makes and success rate — or it could be a blueprint for future opponents.

Perhaps most importantly, the Thunder rendered Wembanyama ineffective offensively for nearly 35 minutes. The Frenchman connected on 10 of his 12 free throws, snagged 13 rebounds and swatted six shots, but missed all but one of his 13 attempts from the field. Some of this can be chalked up to fatigue; Oklahoma City took full advantage of Wemby's obsession with being near the action by constant movement, whether by dribble handoffs or ball screens only to retreat to the perimeter and launch. Observing his performance in totality, though, the Thunder just pounced on him at every chance they got. Even in his fourth NBA season, the Frenchman still has a ways to go in the physicality department, something their rivals boast in spades. Different coverages, mixed in with timed hits and crowding, almost made Wembanyama double- and triple-think situations before reacting.

"I need to go back to playing the basketball I like," Wembanyama said. "I've got no reason to be hesitant, no reason to not be myself. I'm good when I have fun … I was indecisive, overthinking it."

The brilliant — and perhaps terrifying — aspect of the Thunder, something that might have somehow been forgotten amid the Knicks and Spurs craze the basketball world was treated to, is that this team isn't that far removed from an unprecedented regular season and playoff run.

Shai Gilgeous-Alexander was dogged in his delivery, finishing with 32 points on 27 shots, Jalen Williams missed 11 of his 16 attempts, Chet Holmgren wasn't particularly effective offensively and Cason Wallace didn't connect on a single triple. And yet this team, at one point, held a near-30-point lead on the road. On nights when the starters are misfiring, their depth (48 points from the second unit) will carry them. Rookie Aday Mara's bright performance and admirable job defending Wembanyama was a stern indication of general manager Sam Presti's eye for talent, churning out products like a Tulsa aircraft factory in the '90s. This is a group that expects to be there at the end when it's all said and done, even if the finish line is months down the road.

"This game doesn't really mean that much," Gilgeous-Alexander said. "The first game of the season. It just means you used the opportunity tonight to get better against a very good team and we did so. And that's what we try to accomplish every single night in an 82-game season and we did so tonight."

articles.title: Player grades: Thunder bully Spurs on Opening Night in 116-104 win
articles.summary: Player grades for the Oklahoma City Thunder's 116-104 win over the San Antonio Spurs.
articles.body:
SAN ANTONIO — Going with the vicious behind-the-back dribble move, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander had Stephon Castle flustered. In the final seconds of the third quarter, the two-time MVP winner faded and fell. His mid-range jumper swished through. Alongside an and-one call.

The Oklahoma City Thunder capped off 2026-27 NBA Opening Night with a 116-104 win over the San Antonio Spurs . They led for most of the night and by as many as 26 points.

By the opening possessions, the Thunder played with a different energy compared to the 2026 Western Conference Finals. Instead of letting the Spurs out-physical them from the jump, they set the tone. Chet Holmgren went headfirst in his one-on-one matchups with Victor Wembanyama. It was an old-school mano-y-mano situation that has seldom materialized over their NBA journeys.

And then there was Jalen Williams. Thunder fans' largest copium argument of the summer. After missing most of the epic 2026 Western Conference Finals, he returned to show he would've made a difference. A weakside recovery block showed off the defensive prowess he has.

The Thunder had a 34-28 lead after the first quarter. It only took the first dozen minutes to know they had this matchup circled as soon as it was announced for Opening Night. It won't erase what happened in the 2026 NBA playoffs, but it would be a step in the right direction to show they can finally get rid of their Spurs problems.

Once the second quarter rolled around, the Thunder took complete control of the game. A game-altering 25-5 run was cathartic to see unfold if you're an OKC fan. After De'Aaron Fox's flagrant foul for swinging down Holmgren, an NBA-regulated scuffle broke out. The end result also included technical fouls for Wembanyama, Williams, Jaylin Williams and Kenrich Williams.

That was enough to get the juices flowing for the Thunder. They completely dissected the Spurs on both ends. San Antonio's offense eroded to Wembanyama's bailout calls to the free-throw line. Meanwhile, OKC's role players hit all of their outside jumpers. It didn't take long for the lead to get to double-digit points. Gilgeous-Alexander piled on with a turnaround jumper he drilled in.

Before you could even process what happened, the Thunder were up by over 20 points. They had 31 points in the second quarter. That was enough to enter halftime with a 65-44 lead over the Spurs. Just in total control of this one. The San Antonio crowd was in complete shock.

But you knew things were too good to be true if you were the Thunder. I mean, the Spurs knocked you out last year in the 2026 Western Conference Finals. You two are universally viewed as the co-title favorites. Surely, San Antonio had at least one momentum-shifting run in it, right? Right.

That was the start of the second half. The Spurs scored the first nine points. Eventually, that avalanched to getting things within 10 points. Castle made another top-of-the-key 3-pointer. Just like that, the Thunder's once-daunting 26-point lead was dwindled to a mere 68-58 with over eight minutes to go in the third quarter. Plenty of time to make things interesting.

Added as a new character to this ongoing soap opera between the Thunder and Spurs, Aday Mara penciled his first chapter. In a two-play sequence, he denied Wembanyama's alley-oop attempt and then caught his own lob for a superb pair of possessions. The 21-year-old showed he was seldom afraid of the national stage as he played a part in OKC's Opening Night statement.

Losing a good chunk of their lead, Gilgeous-Alexander calmed things down for the Thunder. They still came away with 28 points in the third quarter. That helped them stay at a healthy distance of 93-80. The two-time MVP winner already tallied 28 points. He was the best player on the floor. Meanwhile, Wembanyama couldn't buy an actual field goal as the seven-footer jacked up a ton of perimeter jumpers.

In a last-ditch effort, Dylan Harper tried to carry the Spurs to a comeback. He looked like San Antonio's best player. His relentless drives to the rim turned it into a seven-point contest at one point. But the Thunder shut the door. Gilgeous-Alexander did his usual thing, but Jared McCain joined in on the fun. He made a timely bucket after a timely bucket. Ice in his veins.

The Thunder only scored 23 points in the final frame, but that was enough to walk away with a relatively low-stress win over the Spurs. You can't win an NBA championship in October, but you can certainly dampen your odds with a no-show outing against the team that owned you last year. Thankfully, OKC won't deal with that scary alternate reality. At least not for now.

The Thunder shot 45% from the field and went 14-of-31 (45.2%) from 3. They shot 16-of-20 on free throws. They had 24 assists on 43 baskets. Four Thunder players scored double-digit points.

Gilgeous-Alexander led the way with 32 points and six rebounds. Holmgren had a loud 14 points, seven rebounds and four blocks. Williams tallied 12 points and seven rebounds. McCain was the unlikely hero with 20 points dropped off the bench.

Meanwhile, the Spurs shot 39% from the field and went 10-of-37 (27%) from 3. They shot 22-of-25 on free throws. They had 21 assists on 36 baskets. Five Spurs players scored double-digit points.

Wembanyama had a humane 12 points and 13 rebounds. He shot 1-of-13 from the field. Castle was the best of the bunch with 24 points and seven rebounds. Harper looked sharp in his new role with 18 points, seven rebounds and five assists. Fox had 14 points and seven assists. Keldon Johnson dropped 10 points off the bench.

Great way to start the 2026-27 NBA regular season. I called this the must-win Opening Night — the ultimate sports oxymoron. But considering how last year went for the Thunder against this one pesky opponent, they had to avoid history repeating itself. As I said earlier, it doesn't erase your postseason demons. But it's a step in the right direction.

Your three franchise pillars played like so in Gilgeous-Alexander, Holmgren and Williams. And then you even received some help from your role players. On defense, the Thunder remain as sharp as ever. Wembanyama waddled into one of the more inefficient nights in recent memory. For the first time in a minute, you can say OKC's unicorn two-end seven-footer outplayed him.

Matching up on Castle, Gilgeous-Alexander went for another one-on-one look. Almost in anger that he's been regarded as one of his top stoppers, he drove downhill before jamming on the brakes. A nasty baseline fadeaway jumper feathered through. Not even Wembanyama could jump in time for a weakside block.

Gilgeous-Alexander finished with 32 points on 13-of-27 shooting, six rebounds and four assists. He shot 3-of-7 fom 3 and went 3-of-4 on free throws. He also had three steals and three blocks.

If you're going to comb through the history books, this is your textbook Gilgeous-Alexander masterpiece. He painted another Mona Lisa — but with some extra vendetta behind it. Surely, hearing all of the talk all summer, he had this game circled once it dropped. As OKC's leader, the rest of the Thunder followed suit by punching San Antonio straight in the mouth before it found its cockiness.

Gilgeous-Alexander absolutely dazzled from the jump. He constantly attacked San Antonio with mid-range jumpers. Whether with in-motion pull-up jumpers or methodical step-through turnaround jumpers. One of the greatest scorers ever always finds an angle to let off a highly-difficult jumper he butters through. This was him at the peak of his powers. In a flow state, the Spurs had absolutely no answers for him — something completely different from his putrid Western Conference Finals.

Helping the Thunder get up by over 20 points, Gilgeous-Alexander had 16 points in the first half. But his dozen points in the third quarter were arguably his most important of the game. In that stretch, he calmed the waters down. After a dynamic first half, OKC's offense sputtered and badly needed some hero shots. In came the two-time MVP winner to stiff-arm the Spurs from any serious momentum.

Gilgeous-Alexander absolutely closed the books on the Spurs. At all three levels, too. The outside jumper was frequented more often than usual. With Wembanyama cutting off his drives, he slithered around other areas to still put up a superb-efficient 30-plus points. We're watching one of the game's greats, folks. Appreciate it now as it plays out in real time.

In a size advantage, Holmgren put the ball down. He drove headfirst at Devin Vassell. Once he blew past him, he squared right up at Wembanyama's shot contest. The two basketball giraffes collided in mid-air. Holmgren won that matchup. The early bucket was nice, but the message it sent for the rest of the night was more important.

Holmgren finished with 14 points on 3-of-8 shooting, seven rebounds and two assists. He shot 0-of-1 from 3 and went 8-of-8 on free throws. He also had four blocks.

Starting a new school year, Holmgren isn't going to let Wembanyama bully him again. He stood up for himself and punched back. Just like parents in similar situations, all OKC fans could do was smile. You can't wash away your Western Conference Finals sins in one night, but this was the first step in redemption. Welcome back to playing at an All-NBA level.

From the start, Holmgren carried himself differently. He had an extra moxie to him. For most of the first quarter, he stuck on Wembanyama. Every time he had a chance to switch, he rejected the action. Nope. This was my guy. Seven-footer on seven-footer. The results? One of OKC's most dominant showings against San Antonio in years. Wow. Who would've thought?

The Thunder have overthought themselves into a pretzel with Wembanyama. How do you guard someone with his size and skill? Sometimes, the answer is slapping you across the face. Put your own version of him on him in Holmgren. After all, that's what the NBA world wants to see. That has become one of the best rivalries in recent years. Even if it's the Cold War kind.

This was the absolute best launching point for Holmgren's year. Especially since most view it as a fork-in-the-road moment. Will he learn from his postseason failures or falter from them? Through Opening Night, it looks like the 24-year-old utilized the humiliation ritual as extra motivation to return new-and-improved. You couldn't have drawn up anything better.

Moving over on help, Williams caught Castle by surprise. As the latter tried to go for the poster, the former jumped in the air with him. The All-NBA talent nastily rejected him with a weakside block. I guess the Thunder could've certainly used that type of all-world player at the highest stage last year. Alas. Enough with living in the past.

Williams finished with 12 points on 5-of-16 shooting, seven rebounds and two assists. He shot 1-of-2 from 3 and went 1-of-2 on free throws. He also had one block.

The offense doesn't really jump off the screen, but man, Williams just makes the Thunder better. Plain and simple. On both ends. The defense receives an injection of otherworldly versatility. And the offense gets somebody who can keep the rhythm going as one of their top scorers. Even if he comes up with hilariously missed attempts on ambitious trick shots.

If the Thunder hope to run a well-oiled offense — that grows dependent on Gilgeous-Alexander's Superman-esque shot-making — then Williams has to play a key role in that. Especially when the two-time MVP is off the floor. Zooming out over several years, there's a track record of success. But it's been a minute since the 25-year-old was that guy for OKC. Let's see if he can don the Robin outfit once again.

The Thunder operate on a different level when Williams is hitting on all cylinders. As you saw with some of their game-defining runs that really blew this open. The energy level is just livelier when he's in uniform rather than in street clothes. Perhaps no better example was when he got into the meat of things between Fox and Holmgren following the former's flagrant.

Catching Isaiah Hartenstein's DHO in rhythm, McCain drilled in another outside jumper. This time, it was from way deep. Even with Wembanyama's contest, the 22-year-old knocked it down. On the grand stage of Opening Night, he's proven to love the spotlight.

McCain finished with 20 points on 7-of-9 shooting, two assists and two rebounds. He shot 6-of-8 from 3.

You never ever have to worry about McCain being gun-shy. As the Thunder absolutely cooked the Spurs from the perimeter in the first half, he was one of the faces of the charge. Always on the move, his infinite range has proven to be a weapon the Thunder can lean on in their second-unit lineups. And when he's on the floor with Gilgeous-Alexander, he typically salivates at all the open looks he'll get simply from his gravity.

Once again, McCain was sizzling. He had 11 points in the first half. That was part of an effort where the Thunder surgically took apart the Spurs' top-end defense. His outside jumper was a staple in OKC's offense. They're all his now after the offseason moves they made this past summer. I don't think gluttony exists in his dictionary regarding that.

McCain has been awesome since he arrived in OKC. He's the gunner the Thunder have always had an eye on over the years. He's next in line. What an incredible way to start his third season. Not that long ago, he was fighting for his NBA life in the G League. Now, he's penciled his name several times in this legendary Thunder-Spurs rivalry.

articles.title: Aday Mara Sends Spurs, Victor Wembanyama Into Discomfort With Viral Highlight
articles.summary: The Michigan standout showed why the Thunder turned to him against the Spurs. The post Aday Mara Sends Spurs, Victor Wembanyama Into Discomfort With Viral Hi...
articles.body:
The Oklahoma City Thunder swooped up Aday Mara from the Michigan Wolverines for a clear reason. Countering the rising behemoth Victor Wembanyama and the San Antonio Spurs rose at the forefront.

Safe to say, Mara answered that bell greatly with violent intent. And went viral for the moment that sprouted across the web.

Wemby snatched the soul out of the Thunder one year ago in his NBA Playoffs debut. OKC had no one, not even Chet Holmgren, who could bottle the 7-foot-5 monster.

So that's why Mara arrived via the June draft. Now OKC got a glimpse of Mara's potential against Wemby and the Spurs moving forward thanks to this block.

The national champion timed his jump just right and swatted the dunk attempt with his left hand, considered his off hand. Mara had no time to gloat about the viscous block, though.

Then he hustled down the other end of the floor and finished off the alley oop, capping off that dominating sequence. But Mara's block fired off immediate social media reactions.

Notable Reactions for Aday Mara Thunder Debut

So Mara fired off hefty praise via the social media website X, formerly known as Twitter.

"This kid is legit," posted Legion Hoops on the site.

"OKC got even BETTER with Mara, and they drafted him for these reasons," added the account Courtside Buzz.

Mara's debut impressed NBA insider for ClutchPoints Brett Siegel too.

"Aday Mara stuffs Wembanyama on one end and then gets the basket at the other. The perfect complementary big man next to Chet Holmgren in OKC's frontcourt," Siegel posted . "It's amazing that teams in the NBA let the Thunder get Aday Mara. Just an insanely skilled and high-IQ center who will be a factor for this title contender for the next decade."

How Aday Mara can Impact Future Thunder vs. Spurs Matchups

OKC needed a "Wemby stopper" after watching the French talent dominate the Thunder last season. This Thunder team knows all roads to the Western Conference title now goes through Wembanyama and San Antonio.

So Mara looks like the perfect piece for future battles, as this OKC versus San Antonio rivalry intensifies moving forward. The Wolverines star can do more than counter Wemby with his hands and wingspan, though.

Mara brings deceptively fast feet on the floor and moves like a cornerback playing man coverage on the best wide receiver option. He's unafraid to handle the low post dirty work including playing through contact and grabbing rebounds. His former Michigan coach Dustin May trusted him to handle the rugged work for the champs.

Defense became his calling card for a Michigan team that relied more on Yaxel Lendeborg and Morez Johnson on the offensive end. Looks like OKC head coach Mark Daigneault, Holmgren, even two-time NBA Most Valuable Player Shai Gilgeous-Alexander will embrace the new Wemby counterattack and defensive stalwart Mara.

articles.title: El fabuloso anillo de campeones de los Knicks: ¡Con el Madison dentro!
articles.standfirst: Los jugadores de Nueva York recibieron una innovadora joya por su título
articles.summary: Los jugadores de Nueva York recibieron una innovadora joya por su título
articles.body: A pesar de la derrota, fue una noche muy especial en Nueva York. El Madison ha tardado 53 años en volver a ver una ceremonia de campeón con los Knicks como protagonistas. Estandarte elevado a los cielos y reparto de la joya más preciada del baloncesto mundial. El anillo es una maravilla. Es una joya de casi 800 diamantes y zafiros, que está fabricado en oro blanco y que por supuesto está personalilzado para cada jugador de la plantilla. Pero esconde un detalle que le hace único en diseño en la historia: en su interior se puede encontrar una miniatura del Madison Square Garden. Al girar el bisel interior, una reproducción del exterior y el interior del Madison se eleva desde el centro, con sus detalles arquitectónicos. La novedad en el diseño es que no se trata simplemente de grabar un estadio en el metal: es una pequeña estructura tridimensional que se despliega. Además tiene otros detalles que alimentan un anillo absolutamente extraordinario: 16 diamantes de talla esmeralda que representan las 16 victorias de los Knicks en los playoffs, un diamante de 0,16 quilates integrado en el trofeo Larry O'Brien que recuerda la remontada de 16 puntos en el quinto partido de las Finales contra San Antonio, que decidió el campeonato, la inscripción 'Knicks in Five' recuerda que Nueva York conquistó las Finales en cinco partidos, la inscripción 'World Champions' utiliza 69 puntos de diamantes para conmemorar las victorias totales del equipo durante la temporada regular y los playoffs y el '10 weeks' grabado hace referencia a las diez semanas de sacrificio y dedicación que el propietario James Dolan pidió al equipo durante su recorrido hacia el título. El precio del anillo de cada jugador no se ha hecho público, pero hay una versión que se vende para los aficionados, aunque sólo hay 200 copias a la venta, y que cuesta 20.000 dólares llamado Knicks Premier Championship Ring. No es tan lujoso como el de los jugadores, pero recuerda el premio que se han llevado por el campeonato.
